Ancestry: Gargoyle Heritage: Dhampir Class: Laughing Shadow Magus | Paradox of Opposites Seneschal Witch Age: 229 Backstory Mira had a very long life. Beginning as the unborn twin to her dhampiric sister, somehow not dead but really alive either. Lacking a body to call her own. A trapped soul. Oddly fitting, given their heritage. Mira's only escape from this non-existence was being cast upon a wall, as her sister's living shadow. They both descend from so called "psychic vampires" or so they heard, the magicks her sister gained later in life did nothing but reaffirm that, but it sure was an easy way to explain their circumstance. In a way, they could simply not be without one and the other. Maybe her sister had the literal brains but Mira was the mastermind behind their every move, her consciousness, guide to greater power and magical prowess. Her sister provided being in the moment, corporeal and much needed levity, for the two of them. It also helped that she was pretty to boot, very skilled at talking to people. They made a pretty great team, as best as they could manage, even if her beloved sister took all of the credit at times. Their hard earned work but she was fine for the longest time. That was until they fell hard for the same woman and Mira of course, let her sister take charge. To enjoy what she could never have but the sheet strain this put between them was something that tore them apart. Miriam certainly sought to make that literal, she had enough with having to "share" her every little joy, give it all away. It took a lot of pain, effort, blood, sweat, tears but also, reconciliation and negotiation. Mira and her sister had managed to sever themselves, one from the other, together as it turns out, as a team once more. A gradual process, as Miriam was granted a sad little familiar to embody at first but being corporeal outweighed anything making her uncomfortable. She even revealed herself to her sister's love afterwards and somehow, the three of them made it work. It all worked out in the end and Miriam became more and more real. Day by day, with both occult study, friendships earned and memories made, she gained a body all her own. She became more real than real. But as the years went on and on, her hunger for knowledge and magic was not satisfied, the spring in her step did not falter. Learning to do magicks all on her own, learning to do quite a lot without her sister actually, they sure had less and less time spent together as things moved forward, even less time to share with their wife. Why can't she remember their faces? They kept slowing down, trailing behind her.... By the time she had forgotten their names. The regret crushed her the most, things left unsaid, mistakes made over the decades, so much hurt, and yet. Mira could not stop in her pursuit for higher power by that point, it was all she had left. Alone. Diving into ancient, forbidden tome after forbidden tome. Making pacts with higher powers left and right. Looking at god right in the eye and asking them why? Why all this? -# All she ever wanted was to... Then, she blacked out, Mira can't remember when it happened exactly nor how but yes, she had woken up in unknown lands that she would later come to know as Ao . All Mira could recall was a blurry mess, the night prior. There was laughter though, so much laughter, cruel and wicked. A dreadful feeling that would not leave her, even now. She was lost here, but not alone, for Mira had come with a companion of sorts. A thing she has never known nor seen before but instinctually, she held onto her tiny paws, looked into those beady little eyes and silly little pink horn for a nose. Mira knew at that moment that she could not let go of her now. Her little Luz... She is not sure where the name came from exactly but it was comforting, somehow. In the center of the sun-dappled marble floor, a figure knelt, their form a perfect mirror of the young elf princess who sat sketching by the window. They were both slight, with hair the color of moonlight, and features of such delicate precision they seemed carved from pearl. But where Princess Arianell’s brow was furrowed in concentration on her landscape, her double’s face was a placid, empty pool. “Again,” intoned Master Kairon from the shadows. The court chronomancer was a silhouette against the bookshelves, his features obscured, his voice a dry rustle of parchment. “The conduit is not your will. It is your blood. Feel the legacy in it. Command it.” 9:32 AM ‎ The figure—known in the silent ledgers of the palace as the Prism—lifted a hand. Their fingers trembled, not with fear, but with the effort of channeling a power that was both theirs and not theirs. A faint, golden light shimmered at their fingertips, coalescing into a warm, humming radiance. They pressed the light to a shallow cut on their own forearm, a training wound administered minutes before. The skin knitted together seamlessly under the Heal spell. It was a simple divine cantrip, one any novice acolyte could manage. For the Prism, it was a paradox. The magic felt alien, a divine whisper answering a call from a soul that was never meant to pray, yet it flowed through them with practiced ease. “Adequate,” Kairon said, his voice devoid of praise. It was a statement of fact. “The principle is the same. Now, the other heritage. Your true birthright.” The Prism rose. Arianell glanced up from her sketchpad, offering a small, almost imperceptible smile of encouragement before returning to her work. They were, in many ways, sisters. Raised in the same rooms, taught by the same tutors, dressed in the same clothes. The Prism knew the Princess’s favorite songs, the way she tucked her hair behind her ear when nervous, the secret name she had for her father’s sternest advisor. The Prism knew everything about Arianell, and nothing about themselves. They turned to the other side of the room, where a stern-faced elven woman, Armsmistress Lyra, waited. “Visualize the formula. The threads of force. Not a prayer, a command,” Lyra instructed, her voice sharp as a blade. The Prism focused. This magic was different. It didn’t ask; it obeyed . It was a thrumming power in their veins, a gift forced upon them through years of painful, blood-soaked rituals. They extended a hand, and three shimmering darts of pure force—a Force Barrage —shot across the room, striking a training dummy with sharp, precise thuds. “Good. Now, defense. Reaction. A spellcaster is always a target,” Lyra said. She didn’t raise a weapon. Instead, she muttered a quick phrase, and a small, intensely bright ember of fire— Ignition —flashed into existence at her fingertip, shooting toward the Prism. The Prism’s body tensed to dodge. But in that moment, the world stuttered. A gray streak flashed through their vision, a lock of their own hair bleaching white for a heartbeat. They saw it—the flicker of heat in Lyra’s eyes before she spoke the phrase, the nascent glow of the ember before it left her hand. It was a ghost of a moment, a fractured second out of place. They flinched, a half-second too early. The firebolt grazed their shoulder, singing the fine silk of their tunic. Lyra frowned. “Anticipation is one thing. Flinching at shadows is another. Control yourself.” But from the shadows, Kairon stirred. He stepped into the light, his aged elven features sharp and hungry. He made a note on a hovering slate of crystal. “No, Armsmistress. Not a shadow. A ripple. The temporal dissonance manifests. The subject’s connection to the timestream becomes… pliable. Excellent.” He looked at the Prism not as a student, but as a fascinating, complex equation. The Prism shivered, though the burn on their shoulder was already cooling. *** 9:33 AM ‎ King Elian’s private solar was a place of warmth and sorrow. Sunlight, real and unfiltered, streamed through the arched windows, illuminating a portrait of a laughing Arianell as a child. The King stood before it, his broad shoulders slumped under the weight of his ornate robes. “It feels like a betrayal, Kairon,” he said, his voice low. “Every day, we train her for a lie.” “We train it , your Majesty,” Kairon corrected softly, his hands tucked into his sleeves. “To ensure her survival. The vision was absolute. The Cataclysm will happen. This foreseen disaster on Akiton will claim her life. There is no alternate path. Only this one.” “The child from the Apostae affair…” Elian murmured, his finger tracing the painted smile of his daughter. “To take a life so young, extinguished by our own guards in their zeal… and then to use it so…” “The body was intact. The soul had barely fled. My arts were able to call it back, to anchor it,” Kairon said, his tone clinical. “And in doing so, we began the work. The blood infusions have taken. The vessel is no longer just a doppelgänger. It carries Arianell’s magical signature, her essence. The chrono-infusion rituals proceed. When the moment comes, the transposition will be metaphysically perfect. Whatever the cause of this event, it will be fooled.” Elian turned, his eyes etched with a grief that was both past and future. “And what of the Prism’s fate? After?” Kairon was silent for a long moment. “The energies of the Cataclysm are… chaotic. Unpredictable. But it will have a chance. Infinitely more of a chance than it had lying broken on the marble floor after its parents’ failed infiltration. You did not discard a tool, my King. You offered a second chance at a life, in exchange for a singular, ultimate service.” The King looked back at the portrait, his heart a battlefield of a father’s love and a king’s terrible duty. “I pray you are right, old friend. I pray this is not just a more complex form of damnation.” *** (edited) 9:33 AM ‎ The red sands of Akiton stretched to a rust-colored horizon, under a sky dominated by ice storms glowing in solar winds. The air was thin and cold, carrying the scent of crystal dust and ozone. Hidden within a shielded tent near a rocky outcrop, far from the main diplomatic envoy, the Prism waited. They wore Arianell’s face, her clothes, but they felt none of her confidence. The secret meeting between Sovyrian’s emissaries and the representatives from Apostae was a gamble, a desperate bid for reconciliation with their estranged dark elf kin. The air crackled with tension, thick with millennia of bad blood. Kairon stood beside them, his eyes closed, sensing the flow of time itself. “It is almost time,” he whispered. “The Cataclysm builds. Remember your purpose. You are the shield. The perfect substitute.” He pressed a simple leather bag into their hands. “Hold this. Do not open it. Its purpose will reveal itself only if you succeed.” The Prism clutched the bag, its contents a mysterious weight. Their heart hammered against their ribs. This was it. The culmination of a lifetime of training for a single moment they didn't understand. Suddenly, a scream echoed from the scrying sensor pointed at the meeting site. It was followed by the sizzling crackle of spellfire. An assassination. A rival house from Apostae, seeking to shatter the fragile peace. Chaos erupted. Instinct, drilled into them over countless hours, took over. The Prism’s focus narrowed. They felt the world slow, the edges of their vision fraying with ghostly afterimages. They raised a hand, not to attack, but to defend. They spoke a word of power, and the world stuttered . The assassin’s spell—a lance of pure void—struck Arianell’s chest. And did nothing. It hung there, a pulsating, dark star against the silver of her gown, its terrible consequence delayed . In that impossible, stolen second, Kairon unleashed his great working. “Now!” The Prism felt a sensation beyond pain, beyond tearing. It was the feeling of being unwoven . The red desert of Akiton vanished. For a single, nauseating heartbeat, they were somewhere else. A sun-drenched garden. The scent of blooming night-flowers. The real Arianell, her eyes wide with shock and confusion, standing right before them. Their eyes met. A mirror recognizing its original. Then, the universe screamed. 9:34 AM ‎ The Cataclysm found its anchor. The world dissolved into a kaleidoscope of screaming colors and fractured physics. The Prism was the epicenter, a stone dropped into the pond of reality. They were pulled, stretched, and unmade across the dimensions. They felt the transposition spell snap into place with the force of a dying star, swapping their position with Arianell’s in the instant before the void spell’s delayed effect could trigger the shattering. They had taken her place in every way—in location, and in fate. The last thing they heard was Kairon’s voice, not triumphant, but filled with a strange, final urgency. “Live!” *** (edited) 9:34 AM ‎ Consciousness returned like a slow tide. For a moment, the skin appeared ancient, wrinkled and thin, before snapping back to its youthful, elven perfection. The curse was all that remained. The leather bag lay beside them. Remembering Kairon’s words, their fingers, clumsy with shock, fumbled at the ties and opened it. Since there is some kind of new Runelord Guild, I thought I'll make the Runelord of Envy . ---- Ærindël'nafthiëllé Edasseril Ærindël'nafthiëllé Edasseril was the crown princess of the elves, hailing from the ancient Kingdom of Kyonin. Long before the Thassilonian Empire was even a thought, she crossed paths with a young, visionary human traveler named Xin. Captivated by his ambitions and potential, she accompanied him on his early journeys. To the brilliant but mortal Xin, her complex elven name was a mouthful, so he affectionately dubbed her "Naaft." When Xin eventually forged his empire, he did not forget his companion. He granted her rule over the verdant Peridot Isle and its surrounding lands, naming the territory "Edasseril" in honor of her royal family and her beauty. As she invited her elven kin to help build a utopia of shared art, magic, and craftsmanship, her human subjects—untrained in the flowing elven tongue—adopted Xin's pet name for her. Patient, kind, and deeply charitable, the princess accepted being called "Naaft" without complaint, perfectly content to foster a bond with the humans she sought to elevate. History, written by the short-lived and short-sighted, would later warp this truth. The scholars of Golarion mistakenly recorded Naaft as a bitter human who stole an elven princess’s name out of sheer, covetous spite. The irony is tragic, for in those early days, Naaft truly embodied the virtue of Charity. But her human subjects lacked the elven perspective of time. Her grand, well-meaning bureaucracy slowly crumbled into corruption as petty officials scrambled for short-term gains. Deeply disillusioned by this mortal greed, she abdicated her throne long before the empire's descent into sin. A thousand years later, when Earthfall loomed and the elves retreated to Sovyrian, Naaft refused to flee. Her heart broken long ago by the assassination of Xin, she chose to wait for the end in the realm that still bore her name. But the apocalypse brought a different kind of doom to Edasseril. The upstart runelord Belimarius—who was currently sitting on Naaft’s former throne—triggered a catastrophic malfunction in her runewell, threatening to shatter the region's place in time itself. Unwilling to let her legacy end in a tear in reality, Naaft stepped into the breach. She wove a massive matrix of abjuration magic to contain the runewell’s fallout, bracing herself against the raw arcane backlash. She held that ward for ten thousand years. Over the millennia, her physical elven form burned away, gradually fusing with the very abjuration magic she was channeling until she became a living spell—an entity of pure, sustained warding magic. In the crushing, silent isolation of her vigil, her mind began to warp. The benevolent tenets of her goddess, Lissala, twisted from dutiful charity into harsh, demanding obedience. Naaft’s own spirit mirrored this divine rot. The boundless charity that defined her early rule curdled into a deep, agonizing Envy. She did not covet wealth or petty titles; she envied time . She envied the freedom of mortals who could rest, who had the agency to live their lives, and whose good deeds were not rewarded with a ten-millennium prison sentence. When outside forces finally shattered the runewell’s magic and restored Edasseril to the modern timeline, Naaft’s eternal watch ended. But she was not granted peace. (Now defunct) Backstory: The life of a noble is rarely as glamorous as those outside the levers of power assume. That was the first lesson Sonia learned as firstborn daughter of a small noble family in the city of Cheliax. The second lesson she learned - to stop asking questions. Cheliax was no place for the curious, or those unwilling to bend with the winds of change. And change things did; sometimes for worse, sometimes for better. She learned the noble arts that were necessary - the arts of deception, cunning, and subterfuge. Her true passions, however, had always been in the art of creation. Clashes between other tribes were uncommon, but everyone trained to protect themselves. Many focused on archery, some channeled magic, some employed hit and run tactics, while Elton studies tactics themselves. How to take the most advantage from terrain, how to create openings, and how to tend to wounds. Elton obsessed over new strategies to employ on the field. But, actual battles between tribes were uncommon. He trained and obsessed over strategy relentlessly. He loved the clashes between the other tribes or anything else that tried to pick on the tribe, but soon, the clashes had just… stopped. For years, nothing. Elton wanted more battle experience, so he started thinking. Soon, a thought dawned on him. ‘Why not provide my own experience?.’ Elton began studying magic with the same tomes that the magically-inclined tribe members used, but for a different purpose. He focused on conjuration and animation of flesh. His plan was to use those summons to simulate how his tactics might play out. He kept his studies secretive and very slowly refined his creations. After some time, he got pickier, scrapping creations that he deemed inadequate and signs that something was really off about him were starting to show. A crow grew attracted to Elton and whatever flesh experiments he conjured. Other centaurs always have thought that Elton seemed a little out of place, but with his increasing oddities, they grew more suspicious and started investigating. Elton was soon kicked out of the tribe for toiling with undeath and he walked, near aimlessly. He dawned armor to help conceal his identity as tried to figure out what to do. The crow was still hanging out with him, so Elton eventually named it Fletch. Still, they just walked. Didn’t even see any other tribes out there. It’s like nothing was there to begin with, or they just vanished. Then, he saw a sign. A few arrows and bows and part of a campfire. Once a centaur tribe, but where is everyo- Elton fainted without warning or apparent cause. When he woke up, not anywhere near where he had fallen. Then, he saw a floating island. ‘It should not exist, gravity does not work like that’ he thought. But maybe… he could find purpose up there. He was devastated that not only did his friend die but his family didn't take his side and was instead sent far away from the main house. Although he has servants around to take care of his needs, the disdain that they exude for him, for serving him is pretty apparent. He tucked himself away in a small corner of the mansion. There he read books, more of fairy tales he wished for a friend with all his might every day and every night. One day, he woke up from a lonesome slumber he felt a fluffy stuffed dragon. This stuffed dragon, however, is breathing and sound asleep as well. He closed his eyes and went back to sleeping, never been happier that something, someone is this close to him willingly and holding his small hands. Next time he woke up the stuffed dragon was curiously and expectantly looking at him. He immediately felt a strange new but also comforting and warm connection to this stuffed dragon. Through some research at the great library, he quickly figured out that someone answered his prayers for a friend. TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Iron💪🪨10 -💀🪓5 -🐎🔥12 -🔫🐀3 8/9/2026 5:06 AM @Sheet Checker @Trial Sheet Checker Name: Elegy Ancestry: Human Heritage: Duskwalker Class: Cleric/Fighter Age: 32 Backstory: Grey Row is home to many horrors, not the least of which are the Risen- The result of an ambient and malevolent curse upon the land that causes the dead to rise. Fifty years ago, the Rising nearly wiped out the town, and it was only the timely intervention of the Order of the Pyre that managed to stave off the hordes of undead. Since then, the curse has remained, and its source is yet unclear. Upon convergence, Grey Row was isolated from the bulwark of Chelaxian military that kept the dead at bay, and the local Dottari garrison has since abandoned their posts. The majority of the work now falls to the people themselves, and the Executioners, a cloister of Dammerich's militant faithful. Elegy was always bound for their ranks, as her ashen-hued skin marked her as a duskwalker and thus foe to Grey Row's most dreaded enemies. She has served in this role admirably and with little complaint, and has been instrumental in Grey Row's defense since. She spent her formative years in the cloistered priesthood of Dammerich before eventually learning to swing the axe and donning the black and gold armor of the Executioners of Dammerich, as most knew she eventually would. Recent events, however, have introduced specific difficulties. Introduction into Ao has seen a spike in the Risen, and it has become clear a foreign lich is the culprit, moving in to seize the opportunity to exploit the curse. The recovery of the archon Aetalux has, however, made the undead wary of attacking directly, and Elegy has agreed to be a liaison to Axiom, working for them in exchange for their own help dealing with the problem once and for all. https://i.imgur.com/fvUcmVX.jpeg (edited) 5:06 AM Character is ready on FOundry. Each noon and midnight, Fenghuang would descend from the divine realm to recite Lady Jingxi’s verses, ensuring that her words reached those who sought inspiration and beauty. For centuries, this sacred pilgrimage continued without incident. Until one fateful day, Fenghuang descended into the mortal realm as they had countless times before, only to find themselves inexplicably disconnected from the divine realm. Instead of returning home, Fenghuang found themselves Converged into the world of Ao, cut off from the celestial realm and separated from their beloved master. Their connection to Lady Jingxi was severed, leaving Fenghuang stranded in a world far removed from the goddess they had served for centuries. Though they can no longer return to the divine realm, Fenghuang refuses to let their master’s poetry fade. They continue to recite Lady Jingxi’s verses wherever they travel, hoping that each poem might somehow reach her across the distance between worlds. Now, Fenghuang wanders across Ao as a traveling poet and performer, carrying their master’s words wherever they go. Yet beneath their cheerful performances lies a quiet longing: to understand why they were Converged into Ao, restore their connection to Lady Jingxi, and one day find their way home. TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Skie | S (9) | R (2) | K (2) 8/11/2026 4:39 AM Name: Rika Fukuda Ancestry: Human Heritage: Beastkin Class: Animist / Monk Age: 33 Born to two parents, both vulpine beastkin, Rika spent the earliest years of her childhood knowing little more than a roaring hearth and the warm smiles of her parents. No great tragedy marked her departure from this life. One day, when she was but a girl of four, while she and her parents were stocking up in the markets of Wanshi, she caught the attention of a pair of traveling Tengu monks. They saw something that Rika's parents could not: that Rika's easily distracted nature was not just the wandering thoughts of a child, but the ability to sense the natural spirits of the world. They saw potential in her - a potential they could hone, but only if her family was willing. It was another year until they finally decided to allow it; sending a missive for her to be spirited away to a temple, quietly nestled between twin ranges. There, she spent much of her youth as a scribe, yet at the age of thirteen, the Tengu blademasters of the temple began to test her aptitudes. While not directly having a knack for bladework, she proved a quick study; and cultivating her talent for sensing spirits meant she was a deft hand for magic. Fifteen long years passed before her training was considered complete. It was her time to be sent to maintain a shrine to the goddess Shizuru, not far from the Temple. More time would pass - she would busy herself with the writing of scrolls, the blessing of petitioners, and the maintenance of the shrine. Until one day, as the noontime sun hung in the center of the sky, she found herself staring at a rift in the worlds. Before she could even react, her senses were blinded. A cacophony of sound sent her scattering through the rift, alongside the debris of the stone pathways beneath her. When she landed in Axiom... perhaps by the grace of Shizuru, she landed on her feet. TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Mierrin | 🌊 2 8/12/2026 12:27 AM Name: Mierrin Ancestry: Jotunborn Heritage: Undine Class: Kineticst | Invoker (witch flexible spell caster) Age: 36 Backstory Mierrin Was born in a small community of Jotunborn who lived on an Island. While to them it was simply home, the near by humans called it giant island, which he supposed was an aped enough name if one realized it was refiring to the denizens of the island and not the size of the humble land mass. Conversely his people started calling the island the humans lived on little island, which was sometime a bit confusing given it was a good 100 times larger than giant island. Horrible nomenclature aside, He had a good upbringing with loving parents, an older sister, and a younger brother. He was a bit of an loner, polite, well mannered and likeable enough, though he always seemed a bit, distracted. At a young age, he discovered his supernatural affinity for water. Growing up he spent almost as much time swimming in the ocean around the island than on the island it's self. One day while exploring Mierrin felt a strange calling towards an under water cave. Dove into the cave letting his glowing Iivlar illuminate his way. At it's end he discovered an air pocket that lead into a massive cavern where he discovered an ancient library. There the books and the words called to him and he read and learned. That's how despite growing up on an island in a middle of no where Mierrin was able to obtain a quite thorough education learning, everything from magic to mathematics. It was also in the library where he met his familiar vapor, who has been his loyal and absolutely never obnoxious companion. Once Mierrin reached his 20th year he began to feel that giant island was a bit too small so he ventured out to see the wide world and traveled next door to little island where he discovered that the world at large was actually quite small with annoying low doors and tiny furniture. He eventually found his way to the small nation's capital where he got a job at the royal library. It definitely was because the place felt familiar and not that it was one of the few buildings he could stand up in without hitting his head on the ceiling. There he was well valued because of his intelligence, broad foundation of knowledge, and for his ability to shelve books on the top rows without a ladder. He spent his next decade and a half bouncing between the library making occasional trips home and traveling to new places. It was quite the nice life until both giant island and little island, which actually does have a name, were transported to the plane of AO. It was quite the upset, disrupting trade and people's lives. Vapor suddenly insistent, urged Mierrin to return to the library of his youth. It was there he was greeted with a vision from his patron, a declaration that he should travel to the center of this new plane and discover all he can about this new world. ----------------- Character is on foundry! TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Glennmp | Atlas 13 | Valerian 3 8/14/2026 8:38 AM Name: Valerian Caelith Ancestry: Elf Heritage: Custom Mixed Heritage: Human (don't make fun of me okay :( ) Class: Scoundrel Rogue | Fencer Swashbuckler Age: 26 Might change goading feint into something else I'm not sure yet, need to clarify more on the rules for it ----------------- Backstory: Valerian Veyr was born in Goka, the great city of Tian Xia, to an elven father from the west and a human mother born and raised within the city itself. Goka was unlike any place his father had ever known. Built around one of the few great openings through Qiang Tian, the Wall of Heaven, the city served as a gateway between Tian Xia and the lands beyond the mountains. Travelers, merchants, adventurers, nobles, gamblers, and warriors from across Golarion passed through its streets. To Valerian, Goka was simply home. His father, Veyr, had first arrived in Goka on business. A traveler at heart, he had spent much of his life moving from place to place, following trade routes and chasing the next horizon. He worshipped Desna, believing that life was meant to be experienced rather than merely endured. During his stay in Goka, he met Shindranni, a talented and beautiful drake racer who had grown up among the city's bustling streets and racing grounds. Their meeting quickly became something more. Where Veyr was a wanderer, Shindranni was deeply rooted in Goka. She knew its alleys, markets, temples, racing tracks, and fighting schools. She was fascinated by the sword and held a particular reverence for Setsuna Kuga, the legendary "Perfect Swordswoman" and founder of Minkai. From Shindranni, Valerian inherited a love of the blade and an appreciation for the discipline required to master it. From his father, he inherited something very different. Veyr taught Valerian that not every conflict needed to be won with a sword. Words could be sharper than steel, and a well-timed lie could accomplish what a hundred soldiers could not. To Veyr, the clever warrior was the one who convinced his opponent that they had already lost before the fighting even began. His father's devotion to Desna instilled in him a love of freedom, travel, and the unknown, while his mother's reverence for Tsukiyo and Shizuru taught him the value of reflection, honor, and the pursuit of perfection. As he grew older, Valerian found that none of these beliefs felt contradictory. He eventually came to follow the Path of the Heavens, seeing the divine not as a single path that demanded his obedience, but as a collection of ideals worth striving toward. Desna represented the freedom to wander. Tsukiyo represented contemplation and the quiet wisdom found in darkness. Shizuru represented the discipline and excellence he sought through the sword. Growing up in Goka also gave Valerian an unusual appreciation for the city's dragons, drakes, and kobolds. The city's kobold communities fascinated him, and he spent much of his youth listening to their stories of dragons, ancient treasures, and ancestral heroes. His mother's experience as a drake racer only strengthened that fascination. Valerian learned to recognize individual drakes by temperament and behavior. Eventually, he developed a particular fondness for them. As he grew older, his relationship with Goka's kobolds became more personal. He learned their customs, listened to their stories, and occasionally found himself dragged into their petty disputes. In return, they taught him things no formal instructor could: how to recognize a lie from a dragon's servant, how to read the movement of a frightened drake, and perhaps most importantly, how never to underestimate something simply because it was smaller than himself. 8:39 AM Valerian's martial training eventually brought him under the tutelage of the Butterfly Blades of Nai Yan Fei, the Empress of Goka. He learned that the best way to defeat an enemy was often to make them believe they had discovered the perfect opportunity to defeat you. And when they took the bait, Valerian struck. His skill with the sword grew alongside his talent for deception, eventually producing a fighting style that was as much performance as it was combat. As a personal challenge, he undertook the journey along Qiang Tian, the Wall of Heaven. The enormous mountain range seemed almost impossible to comprehend. To Valerian, that was precisely why he needed to walk it. He traveled along its paths alone, sometimes for days without speaking to another person. He slept beneath the stars, meditated in secluded places, and practiced his sword forms until his muscles ached. He meditated for hours, attempting to discover the inner reservoir of strength described by the martial traditions he had encountered. Sometimes he experienced strange visions. Once, while meditating beneath an open night sky, he swore he saw a second set of stars reflected beneath his closed eyes—stars that did not exist above him. Valerian's childhood had been spent watching the Ruby Phoenix Tournament. He remembered sitting beside his parents as a child, barely able to contain himself as legendary warriors entered the arena. He watched the crowds roar, the fighters clash, and the city's gamblers wager fortunes on warriors they had never met. He watched the drake races with the same fascination. Goka was a city where anything could become a spectacle, and Valerian loved it. As he grew older, the Ruby Phoenix Tournament became more than entertainment. It became an aspiration. One day, he wanted to stand among those warriors. And so, during the latest Ruby Phoenix Tournament, Valerian finally found himself there amongst the participants. 8:39 AM For all his preparation, nothing could have prepared Valerian for what happened next. The tournament was interrupted by the arrival of Mogaru, the Final King. The enormous kaiju descended upon Goka, turning celebration into chaos in moments. Buildings shook, crowds scattered, the roar of the creature drowned out everything else. Valerian stood frozen for only a moment. He reached for his sword; there were people in danger! His city was under attack!! He had spent his entire life training for moments like this. Valerian began to run toward the chaos. And then reality broke. There was no explosion. No spell. No warning. One moment he was standing in Goka. The next, the world around him rippled like a reflection disturbed by a stone. Valerian stumbled. The streets stretched impossibly far away; the sounds of Goka became distorted and distant. He caught glimpses of things that could not possibly be there—strange structures, unfamiliar skies, distant figures, and places that seemed to exist somewhere beyond the boundaries of the world. For a moment, Valerian saw Goka. Then he saw somewhere else. Then Goka again. His body felt as though it were being pulled in opposite directions. His armor grew unbearably heavy. His sword seemed impossibly distant. He could hear voices, though he could not understand them. Then came the pressure. An overwhelming force pressed against him from every direction, as though the universe itself were attempting to decide where he belonged. Valerian tried to fight it. Then everything went dark. When Valerian opened his eyes again, Goka was gone. He found himself lying beneath an unfamiliar sky, surrounded by a world that seemed to obey rules he did not understand. He slowly rose to his feet. His sword was still at his side. His armor was still intact. He was still himself. But something had changed. He could feel it. He had been pulled from Golarion and brought somewhere beyond anything his parents, his teachers, or even the dragons of Goka had ever described. It took time to learn the name of the place. Ao. And for the first time in his life, the wanderer who had always dreamed of seeing what lay beyond the horizon found himself somewhere that no traveler from Golarion had ever meant to reach. 8:40 AM @Sheet Checker Valerian is uploaded to the foundry and rdy to be reviewed, ty <3 :) 8:42 AM oh shit I actually havent done my equipment yet Glennmp | Atlas 13 | Valerian 3 8/14/2026 8:53 AM ok its good now Krax - Soot12/Sim11/Tess8/Crane9 8/14/2026 4:42 PM @Glennmp | Atlas 13 | Valerian 3 What is your primary deity? As an explosion knocked both parties down, he moved closer, but as he did, reality on all planes rippled, and broke. Once his vision cleared, he found himself on the Material Plane, in his physical form, with the small dragonet laying nearby. He would've left and shifted back to the Boneyard, but something kept him there. A weird connection to the dragonet. He would need to see what this might be, but first and foremost, he needed to deposit him in a safe place. This hulking man has massive strength and dexterity, a true paragon of physical prowess, and thus many believed he would go on to achieve wonderful things, perhaps even achieve legendary status. One fateful day, he went with some students to a forest for training, but the place happened to suffer a Convergence event. Waking up in an unknown land, he journeyed for a while, protecting his students, until they reached a settlement, where his students could stay safely. Now a bit more familiarized with this strange new world, and understanding others shared a story similar to his, he found camaraderie in this organization of adventurers. He actually enjoyed his brief adventuring journey, and took this event of being stranded in another world as an opportunity to grow his legend. Thus, he decided to become a full-fledged adventurer, where he could further his training, become the greatest warrior possible, and also protect and guide others. TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Beeees|Ty15|BB6|C11|BE5|K3 8/24/2026 5:05 PM Name: Karrik Ancestry: Human Heritage: Aiuvarin Class: Fighter/Ranger Age: 27 A handsome male half-elf, marred by a beast’s claws. A born monster hunter and ranger, Karrik has dedicated his life to the preservation of Ao’s native wildlife against rapidly changing threats, rampant mutation, and the disruption of the ecosystem by forces both wild and civilized. Karrik has been ordered by his patron to join the Axiomites to serve as a representative of The Knights of The Fey Unicorn and to gauge the interests of the Watcher, whom The Fair Lady suspects to be partly responsible for convergences. Karrik recalls little of his own history, having given it up as part of his devotion to The Fair Lady. Born to a small community in the south of Ao, Karrik’s journey began as a young scout, placing trail markers and warning signs for travelers while more experienced hunters and rangers kept dangers from the roads. As boring as it might be, Karrik’s job was no less important for the civilized folk of Ao. However, the convergence is as unpredictable as the dangers it brings. TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Yozozo | 'Rethy' 9 | Kassidy 5 8/29/2026 9:24 PM Name: Victoria Hoshimi Ancestry: Kitsune Heritage: Dark Fields Kitsune Class: Commander | Wizard Age: 25 Backstory Background: Part of me knew, even before I turned the card over, that I had made a mistake. I felt myself falling through that infinite darkness. I tried to speculate, for a time, where I might land, but eventually I gave up. Conjecture was futile, for I was like a leaf tossed about in the mightiest of hurricanes, or a twig lost into the vast sea. Anxiously I started to worry where I might land, where I might end up, but as I tumbled through the void those fears passed, and I started to worry I may never land, lost in the great astral sea or whatever this place was. I entertained myself for a time, pondering the mysteries of the universe, the life that I once had, the adventure and excitement. Soon I longed for it. I started to long for anything. I thought I would starve to death or dehydration, but that fear was short lived, for I did not feel hunger, nor thirst. I could practice my magic still, casting spells in vain that something, perhaps, may break me free of this place, but nothing I cast had any effect. Nothing I did had any effect. Sleep, meditation, the starry expanse. There was nothing to do or worth doing. I do not know how long I had been tumbling through the void, when almost impossibly there appeared a tear before me. I do not know if I slowed or it if followed me, or perhaps I had never truly been following, but I reached through. Anything. Anything to escape this place. Born as the fourth daughter to the Emperor of the realm, Victoria was never truly destined for anything great. She was disfavored from birth, the Emperor having felt decieved by Victoria's mother as to her Kitsune nature, never had much to do with the child. Isolated, not allowed to associate outside of the palace, Victoria struggled to find her place in that world. So she studied, warfare, magic, whatever she could, in any way to find some meaning and a place for herself. Eventually she was sent off to a wizarding college, with the hopes that she would come back 'useful' to the court. Instead, she found herself encountering a band of adventurers who made her an offer she couldn't refuse. She escaped with them, and they went on many daring adventures, including finding, and raising, a Tyrannosaur. Her knowledge of tactics and warfare helped to guide the group, of which she soon became an invaluable part of. All good things must come to an end, however. The party's greed overtook them, and when they discovered a Deck of Many Things, she could not help but draw. The Donjon. Cursed, banished, and sent to drift in the astral void with nothing but her imagination, she awaited the long eons for something to happen, her magic and skill slowly leeching out over the possible centuries. And then one day that void she was in was breached, and she escaped to land near Axiom. ----------------- Character is uploaded and ready to review on the Foundry Server thank you @Sheet Checker 9:24 PM (Arts!) TicketTool.xyz - Ticketing without clutter Maxi | Nabuk 10 8/31/2026 9:00 AM Greetings! I'm creating this ticket to rebuild Helios (who has 3 XP) into a different character, Torvald. Classes: Empiricism Investigator / Multi-element Kineticist Ancestry: Aiuvarin Android Background: Magical Misfit Backstory: Torvald is a cheerful, ambitious guy, with an aspiration to improve the quality of life of the people around him. In his mind, together people can achieve more than alone. But his clan were on a different opinion, who favoured competition with the other clans instead of cooperation. He was one of the main architects, responsible for building houses, stables, foundries, armouries, walls, tunnels, and other buildings for the city. He took pride in his work, although it just fuelling the endless war, he thought if he does a better job the war will end sooner. But despite all his contribution and hard work, his clan were on the losing side. Little by little, the other clans chipped away from their land. On a fateful night, soldiers of the enemy clan came, pillaging the city. Torvald with his kin had to flee into a nearby mine for safety, but the vengeful raiders didn't rest, they wanted to collapse the mine onto their heads. The miners tried to guide Torvald and the other the survivors to the deeper parts of the mine, in hopes of not immediately dying due to the explosives. Just when they gathered themselves together, a chain of loud explosions trembled the walls. Boulders fell from the ceiling, the first one right above Torvald. As it almost squashed him, it suddenly stopped in place midair. With a perplexed look, he quickly moved away from the way just before the boulder smashed down into the ground. He didn't knew how he did it, but he quickly tried the same with the others, saving them from the collapse. They were all safe, but trapped deep underground. 9:00 AM After a while, they experienced a strange feeling. It's... wind? Underground? How if the tunnels collapsed? Not knowing what to do, they went into the direction of the wind. Strangely they soon saw a light of the end of the tunnel. Could be some kind of bioluminescent monster who lures their prey with light? Should they just wait here until the monster goes away? But Torvald went further, and despite all possibility, he found an exit to the surface. How? They were deep underground, there shouldn't be any kind of exit to the surface this deep. Later they found out that they are now in Ao. With his old home in ruins and no way back, he made himself comfortable in his new home, Axiom. With his newfound powers of summoning and manipulating different elements, his architect capabilities grew tenfold, what he previously could do in a week now he can do in mere hours, quickly building new homes for his survived brethren. Now he spends his time as an adventurer, refining his skills in the vastness of the unknown. 9:01 AM 9:03 AM (Additionally I will want to use all 13 option A on Torvald, but I assume that would be better in a separate ticket.) I was stuck between dwarf and android, and ended up making an android. Maxi | Nabuk 10 9/1/2026 6:44 PM Would the below be a good expansion of the backstory? There was once an old elf Almer, master of magic, alchemy, and craftsmanship. He lived in a small village on the outskirts, and spent his time on his experiments. Once he wandered far and wide, discovering the secrets of world, but his now brittle and frail body can't withstand long trips anymore. His biggest fear is realised, despite having the lifespan of an elf, he is ageing. He doesn't have an apprentice to pass down his knowledge to, but it would be a shame to bring hundreds of years of knowledge to the grave, so he decided to take matters into his own hands. Loathing the concept of ageing, he committed to something bold: creating a new, synthetic person, whom doesn't have to deal with becoming old. Even if he has to endure the experience of ageing, at least someone else can enjoy eternal youth. Filled with determination he got to work, using all his craftsmanship to create the perfect vessel: bones made out of steel, alchemical blood resistant to poison and disease, and his latest discovery: incorporated bioluminescent lines through the body, which can temporarily empower him beyond normal capabilities in critical times of need. Looked like just a real elf on the outside. But despite all the excellence this synthetic body can give, it is just an empty vessel after all, nothing more than a place for someone to inhibit. It didn't had a soul. Yet. 6:44 PM He didn't wanted any conventional necromancy, no illusions of a person, he wanted the real deal: a new soul, directly from the creation's forge. So he begun his last quest: Seeking out an old ritualist whom may help him establish a connection to the positive plane. They gathered rare materials, wrote esoteric symbols in complex shapes on a huge circle, put the body in the middle, and began the ritual. They chanted, burned the incense, and bright waving light floated around as the environment started to blur away, temporarily intersecting the two planes, to be at two places at once, creating a seamless gateway to move through. Colourful floating orbs started to appear around them, souls of freshly created from creation's forge. They successfully established the connection, but will a soul willingly claim this body? So they continued to keep up the ritual while they waited for a soul to come. They waited and waited, their doubt increased by the minute. But just before they thought they failed, a little but bright green orb floated around the body. After a moment which felt like an eternity, the orb assimilated into the body, his bioluminescent lines lit up, and Torvald was born. With the help of Torvald, Almer could once again experience the beauty of the world. Torvald showed him the wonderful in the ordinary, cultures in faraway places, things that didn't exist just a few decades ago. They grew closer together, and in two hundred years Torvald studied and became an architect of his clan. He eventually earned a place at the Synostosis Academy in Yled, where he studied academia, medicine, magic, and necromancy. He graduated not merely as a competent necromancer, but as a meticulous scholar of anatomy and the occult. His education brought him to Graydirge, where he apprenticed under a halfling coroner responsible for the city's ossuary. His mentor taught him the practical realities of Geb's relationship with the dead, but also impressed upon Markkus a lesson his academy instructors had largely ignored: every corpse had once belonged to someone who mattered. When his mentor eventually died, Markkus was ordered to prepare the halfling's body for labor in the fields. For the first time, he found himself unable to accept the fate awaiting the dead. With the quiet assistance of several agents of the Pathfinder Society, Markkus arranged for his mentor's corpse to be smuggled out of Graydirge so that he might receive a proper burial beyond Geb's borders. They never reached their destination. (edited) Shattered Convergence Tracker 1:57 AM Something happened on the road. Markkus remembers fragments — a pursuit, a strange light, his mentor's name spoken aloud, and a sensation as though the world itself had briefly come undone. Then there was darkness. When Markkus awoke, he was somewhere else. Somewhere new, not found in the books lining the dusty shelves of his library. Armed with little more than his intellect and abilities - Markkus struggles with the transition from forensics to adventuring, finding it odd and uncomfortable to associate moreso with the living.
